title: What is a satisfaction survey?
summary: Learn what a satisfaction survey is, how it works, and which types to use. See how contact center managers turn customer feedback into better service.
body_markdown:
A satisfaction survey is a structured questionnaire that measures how well an interaction, product, or service met a customer's expectations. A customer ends a 20-minute call, your agent moves straight to the next queue, and nobody learns whether that conversation solved the problem or created a new one. Contact center managers regularly face this gap, and[Zoom Contact Center](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/contact-center/) helps close it by letting you send customizable surveys after customer interactions and analyze the feedback to understand satisfaction and improve the customer experience.


This guide defines the satisfaction survey, compares the main survey types, and explains how each one fits a contact center workflow, from the first question to the final report. You'll also find a decision framework for choosing a survey approach, practical use cases for your team, and answers to common questions from contact center managers.

## What is a satisfaction survey?


A customer satisfaction survey is the same tool, applied to the customers you serve. It typically pairs a rating question with an open-ended question that explains the score.


A satisfaction survey is a structured questionnaire that measures how well a product, service, or interaction met a customer's expectations, giving service teams direct feedback they can act on.


Customer satisfaction score (CSAT) is the metric many teams calculate from these surveys. It divides the number of satisfied responses by total responses and multiplies the result by 100. Because CSAT reflects a single moment, contact centers usually collect it right after a call, chat, or video interaction.


Zoom Contact Center applies this approach with engagement surveys, which collect feedback after voice or video interactions so managers can see how customers rated specific conversations. For a deeper look at the metrics around it, see our guide to[contact center experience](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/contact-center-experience/) .


## How does a satisfaction survey work?


Here's how to create a satisfaction survey in seven steps:


1. Define the decision the survey should inform, such as coaching priorities or queue staffing.
2. Choose the survey type: a CSAT survey for one interaction, Net Promoter Score for loyalty, or customer effort score for ease.
3. Write one core rating question and keep follow-up questions focused on that goal.
4. Pick a rating scale, such as one to five, and use it consistently across channels.
5. Add one open-ended question so each rating comes with a reason.
6. Send the survey soon after the interaction, in the channel where it happened.
7. Review scores and comments by queue, channel, and agent group, then act on the patterns.


Choose the survey type based on the question you need answered. A CSAT survey measures satisfaction with one interaction. Net Promoter Score (NPS) measures how likely customers are to recommend you. Customer effort score (CES) measures how easy it was for customers to get their issue resolved. Many contact centers pair CSAT with a second metric, since each one shows a different part of the customer experience.


In Zoom Contact Center, administrators can design surveys with multiple-choice and open-ended questions and link them to voice or video queues, which keeps the survey tied to the interaction it describes. For question ideas, see these[customer service survey question examples](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/customer-service-survey-questions/) .

## How to choose a satisfaction survey


Choosing a satisfaction survey approach is easier when you evaluate it against how your contact center operates. Use these six criteria as a checklist:


1. **Match the survey to the decision.** Pick the survey type based on what you will change, such as coaching plans, queue staffing, or self-service flows.
2. **Check channel coverage.** Confirm the survey can follow customers across the channels you use, such as voice and video queues, so channels are measured consistently.
3. **Write satisfaction survey questions for contact centers that fit the interaction.** Ask about resolution, wait time, and agent helpfulness rather than general brand sentiment.
4. **Plan the timing.** Decide whether the survey goes out right after the interaction or after a set delay, and test which fits each queue.
5. **Define who sees results.** Set permissions so supervisors, quality teams, and administrators see the data they need and nothing more.
6. **Build a follow-up process.** Assign owners who review low scores, contact customers when appropriate, and report trends to leadership. Zoom Contact Center surveys link to queues and feed contact center analytics, which supports this review.


> Key questions to ask any vendor: Which queues and channels can a survey link to, and how are permissions for viewing results managed?


Score each criterion from one to five for the options you compare, and weight the ones that matter most to your queues. A survey that scores well on criteria one, five, and six helps your team move from feedback to action.

## Satisfaction survey use cases for contact centers


Satisfaction surveys create value when they connect to a decision. These five use cases show where contact center teams apply them.


- **Post-call service quality:** Surveys linked to voice or video queues in Zoom Contact Center let managers see how customers rate individual conversations and compare results across teams. Low scores point to the interactions worth reviewing first.
- **Agent coaching:** Supervisors pair satisfaction scores with[call recordings or transcripts](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/quality-management/) to find strong examples and training opportunities. Coaching decisions stay with people, and survey data gives those conversations specific evidence.
- **Self-service feedback:** A short survey after a virtual agent conversation shows whether customers found answers without waiting for a person. Zoom Virtual Agent offers a Customer Satisfaction Survey skill for this purpose, and a look at[how AI reshaped customer experience at Zoom](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/from-reactive-to-proactive-how-ai-reshaped-our-customer-experience-at-zoom/) shows how teams think about the shift.
- **Queue and staffing reviews:** Comparing scores by queue and time of day can show where long waits or complex issues affect satisfaction. Those patterns inform routing and[staffing reviews](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/workforce-management/) .
- **Customer recovery:** A low score can trigger a manager review and a follow-up call while the concern is still fresh. Customers see that feedback leads to a response, which can build trust.


To analyze survey results alongside other customer data, read about[running your business with CX data](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/running-your-business-with-cx-data/) or explore[Zoom CX Insights](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/cx-insights/) .

## Satisfaction survey FAQs


### What is a satisfaction survey?


A satisfaction survey is a structured questionnaire that asks customers to rate and explain their experience with a product, service, or interaction. Businesses use the results to track satisfaction over time, find service gaps, and decide what to improve. Many surveys combine a numeric rating question with one open-ended question, which adds the reason behind each score.


Surveys differ by purpose. Transactional surveys follow a specific interaction, while relationship surveys check sentiment across a longer period. Choosing between them depends on whether you want to evaluate one conversation or understand the broader customer relationship.


### How does Zoom Contact Center send a satisfaction survey?


Zoom Contact Center engagement surveys let administrators create surveys with multiple-choice and open-ended questions, then link them to voice or video queues. Based on queue settings, the survey can reach customers after the agent ends the call or after a set time. Supervisors can then review results in contact center analytics. See the current Zoom support documentation for permission details.


Zoom Virtual Agent also offers a Customer Satisfaction Survey skill in the AI Studio skill library, which administrators can add to virtual agents. Review survey settings in the Zoom support documentation before launch, because available options depend on your license and queue configuration.


### What is the difference between CSAT and NPS?


CSAT measures satisfaction with a specific interaction, while Net Promoter Score (NPS) measures how likely customers are to recommend an organization. CSAT usually uses a short rating scale after a call, chat, or purchase. NPS typically uses a zero-to-10 scale and fits relationship tracking over time, so the two metrics answer different questions and can complement each other.


Customer effort score (CES) adds a third view by asking how easy it was to resolve an issue. Teams often choose one primary metric for each stage of the customer journey and add a second only when it answers a question the first cannot.


### When should you send a satisfaction survey?


Send a satisfaction survey soon after the interaction, ideally within 24 hours, while the experience is still fresh. Waiting several days can reduce recall and make the feedback less specific. For relationship surveys, some organizations choose a quarterly or twice-yearly schedule, which helps limit asking the same customers too often and gives enough time to act on earlier results.


In a contact center, timing also depends on the channel. A survey after a phone or video call can go out right away, while a survey after a multi-day email thread may work better once the case closes.


### How do you increase satisfaction survey response rates?


Shorter surveys can earn more responses, so limit the survey to one rating question and one open-ended follow-up. Send it through the channel where the interaction happened, use plain language, and explain how feedback will be used. Testing the survey on mobile devices before launch also helps, because many customers will open it on a phone.


Track completion and abandonment by queue and channel. If one queue shows noticeably lower completion, review the wording, length, or delivery timing for that queue first.
